title: 2020 年全国硕士研究生招生考试 英语（二）

sections.title: Section I　完形填空
sections.dir: Read the following text. Choose the best word(s) for each numbered blank and mark A, B, C or D on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)
sections.note: 主线：做好父母难在“有耐心”，失控的代价与补救。3、12 两处逻辑连词最易凭语感选错。

paras.en: Being a good parent is, of course, what every parent would like to be. But defining what it means to be a good parent is undoubtedly very 1 , particularly since children respond differently to the same style of parenting. A calm, rule-following child might respond better to a different sort of parenting than, 2 , a younger sibling.
paras.zh: 做个好父母，当然是每位父母都想要的。但界定“好父母”的含义无疑非常 1 ，尤其因为孩子们对同一种育儿方式的反应并不相同。一个安静、守规矩的孩子，对另一种育儿方式的反应，可能比 2 年幼的弟妹更好。

paras.en: 3 , there's another sort of parent that's a bit easier to 4 : a patient parent. Children of every age benefit from patient parenting. Still, 5 every parent would like to be patient, this is no easy 6 . Sometimes parents get exhausted and frustrated and are unable to maintain a 7 and composed style with their kids. I understand this.
paras.zh: 3 ，还有另一种类型的父母，稍微容易 4 一些：有耐心的父母。无论哪个年龄段的孩子，都能从耐心的育儿方式中受益。不过，5 每位父母都愿意有耐心，这却不是一件容易 6 的事。有时父母会疲惫、沮丧，无法以 7 而沉着的态度对待孩子。这一点我理解。

paras.en: You're only human, and sometimes your kids can 8 you just a little too far. And then the 9 happens: You lose your patience and either scream at your kids or say something that was a bit too 10 and does nobody any good. You wish that you could 11 the clock and start over. We've all been there.
paras.zh: 你只是凡人，有时孩子就是能把你 8 得有点过头。然后 9 的事就发生了：你失去了耐心，冲孩子大喊，或者说了一些过于 10 、对谁都没有好处的话。你希望自己能 11 时钟、从头再来。我们都经历过这些。

paras.en: 12 , even though it's common, it's important to keep in mind that in a single moment of fatigue, you can say something to your child that you may 13 for a long time. This may not only do damage to your relationship with your child but also 14 your child's self-esteem.
paras.zh: 12 ，尽管这很常见，但有一点务必记住：在疲惫的一瞬间，你可能对孩子说出一些你会 13 很久的话。这不仅可能损害你和孩子的关系，还会 14 孩子的自尊。

paras.en: If you consistently lose your 15 with your kids, then you are inadvertently modeling a lack of emotional control for your kids. We are all becoming increasingly aware of the 16 of modeling tolerance and patience for the younger generation. This is a skill that will help them all throughout life. In fact, the ability to emotionally regulate or maintain emotional control when 17 by stress is one of the most important of all life's skills.
paras.zh: 如果你总是对孩子失去 15 ，那你就在无意中给孩子示范了情绪失控。我们都越来越清楚地意识到，为年轻一代示范宽容与耐心的 16 。这是一项能让他们终身受益的技能。事实上，在被压力 17 时仍能调节情绪、保持情绪控制，是所有生活技能中最重要的一项。

paras.en: Certainly, it's incredibly 18 to maintain patience at all times with your children. A more practical goal is to try, to the best of your ability, to be as tolerant and composed as you can when faced with 19 situations involving your children. I can promise you this: As a result of working toward this goal, you and your children will benefit and 20 from stressful moments feeling better physically and emotionally.
paras.zh: 当然，要始终对孩子保持耐心，是极其 18 的。更实际的目标是：尽你所能，在面临 19 的、涉及孩子的局面时尽可能宽容、沉着。我可以向你保证：朝着这个目标努力，你和孩子都会受益，并会从充满压力的时刻中 20 出来，身心状态都更好。

items.exp: 定位首段第二句 But defining what it means to be a good parent is undoubtedly very ___。空后 particularly since children respond differently to the same style of parenting 正是在解释“为什么难以界定”，故 tricky（棘手的、难对付的）。A tedious（单调乏味的）说的是事情本身枯燥，与“难以定义”不是一回事；C instructive（有教益的）与 B pleasant（令人愉快的）都是褒义评价，与 But 的转折及“没有统一标准”的语境相反。

定位 A calm, rule-following child might respond better to a different sort of parenting than, ___ , a younger sibling。空格夹在逗号之间作插入语，后面的 a younger sibling 是举出的“另一个孩子”，用来印证前句“孩子反应各异”，故 for example。A in addition 表并列补充，但此处不是另起一层；C at once（立刻）表时间、D by accident（偶然）表方式，都与“举例”无关。

定位第二段首句 ___ , there's another sort of parent that's a bit easier to 4 : a patient parent。上段刚说“好父母难以界定”，本句转而提出一种“较容易描述”的类型，是消极之后的积极转折，故 Fortunately。C Accordingly（因此）表因果，可上句推不出“还有另一种父母”；D Eventually 表时间上的最终；B Occasionally（偶尔）是频率，都不合。

定位 another sort of parent that's a bit easier to ___ : a patient parent。冒号后的 a patient parent 正是对前文的“说明”，且与上段 defining what it means 同义复现，故 describe。A amuse（逗乐）、D train（训练）都无法与冒号后的名词构成“界定、描述”关系；B assist（帮助）更无逻辑落点。
定位 Still, ___ every parent would like to be patient, this is no easy 6。前半句承认“父母都愿意有耐心”，后半句却转出“这并不容易”，是让步关系，while 意为“尽管”。B because 会把因果说反（“都想有耐心”不能解释“不容易”）；C unless 表否定条件，句意颠倒；D once（一旦）表条件时点，此处无此逻辑。
定位 this is no easy ___。this 回指 to be patient，即“保持耐心”这件事本身；no easy task 是固定表达，意为“不是轻松的任务”。A answer（答案）与“有无耐心”不搭；C choice 会把“有没有耐心”降格为“选不选”；D access（获得、接触）常接 to sth，此处无介词，结构上也不成立。

定位 unable to maintain a ___ and composed style with their kids。空格与 composed（沉着镇定的）并列，二者共同描述“对待孩子的态度”，且全段主题是耐心，故 tolerant（宽容的），与 patient 同义呼应。B formal（正式的）说的是场合礼节；C rigid（僵化的）带贬义，与 composed 的正面色彩冲突；D critical（批评的）与“宽容”正相反。
定位 sometimes your kids can ___ you just a little too far。push sb too far 是固定搭配，意为“把某人逼得太过分”，与下文“你失去耐心”构成因果。B drag 虽也有“强拉”义，但指身体上的拖拽；A move（移动）与 D send（送出）都无法与 too far 组成“逼迫”的意思，也解释不了情绪失控。
定位 And then the ___ happens: You lose your patience...。冒号后就是“失去耐心”这一具体表现，而上段已交代父母疲惫、孩子逼人，故这种失控是“不可避免的”，inevitable。A mysterious（神秘的）与“人之常情”相悖；B illogical（不合逻辑的）否定其合理性；C suspicious（可疑的）修饰“事情发生”不通。

定位 say something that was a bit too ___ and does nobody any good。空格与 scream at your kids 并列，且 does nobody any good 说明这话伤人，故 harsh（刻薄严厉的）。A boring（无聊的）说的是趣味，与“伤害”无关；B naive（幼稚的）评价的是说话人的判断力；D vague（含糊的）也无法推出“对谁都没好处”。

定位 You wish that you could ___ the clock and start over。turn back the clock 是固定表达，意为“让时光倒流”，与 start over（重新来过）互为呼应。B take apart（拆开）是具体的机械动作，与“时钟”只作字面搭配；C set aside（搁置）与 D cover up（掩盖）都推不出“回到过去、重新开始”的意思。

定位 ___ , even though it's common, it's important to keep in mind...。even though it's common 先让步承认“这很常见”，主句却强调“务必记住会造成伤害”，前后是转折，故 However。A Overall 用于总结上文，而此处是往下递进；B Instead 表替代，前文并无被替代的做法；D Otherwise 表“否则”，需要前句为条件或禁令。
定位 you can say something to your child that you may ___ for a long time。上文说这是“疲惫一瞬间”说出口的话，下文说它伤关系、伤自尊，可见这句话会让人“后悔很久”，故 regret。A like 与语境相反；B miss（错过、思念）与 C believe（相信）都无法接 for a long time 表示“长期懊悔”。

定位 not only do damage to your relationship with your child but also ___ your child's self-esteem。not only...but also 表递进，空格须与 do damage 同向，宾语又是 self-esteem，故 affect（损害、影响）。A raise（提升）方向正相反；C justify（证明……正当）与“伤害自尊”不搭；D reflect（反映）不含“造成损害”义。

定位 If you consistently lose your ___ with your kids。lose one's cool 是固定搭配，意为“发脾气、失去冷静”，与上文的 lose your patience 同义复现。A lose one's time、C lose one's race 都不成搭配；B bond（纽带）虽可与 lose 连用，但“失去纽带”推不出下文“给孩子示范情绪失控”。

定位 We are all becoming increasingly aware of the ___ of modeling tolerance and patience。紧接着的 This is a skill that will help them all throughout life 在说这件事“有价值、有益终身”，故 importance。A nature（本质）只回答“是什么”，接不上“有益终身”；B secret（秘诀）、D context（背景）与 aware of the...of 结构搭配生硬，也不承接下文。

定位 maintain emotional control when ___ by stress。be confronted by/with sth 意为“面对（压力、困难）”，与 stress 搭配最自然，也照应上文 exhausted、frustrated、fatigue 这些压力源。A cheated（被欺骗）与“压力”不搭；B defeated 把压力说成“击败人”，与“仍能调节情绪”矛盾；C confused 不能与 by stress 构成固定表达。

定位 Certainly, it's incredibly ___ to maintain patience at all times with your children。下一句 A more practical goal is... 说明原目标不现实，可见“始终有耐心”是“极难的”，故 hard。A terrible（糟糕的）评价对象错位——难的是这件事，不是它“坏”；C strange、D wrong 都无法解释“为什么要退而求其次”。
定位 when faced with ___ situations involving your children。上文反复讲孩子把父母逼得太狠、父母因此失控，可见这些情形是“考验人的、难对付的”，trying situations 正是此义。B changing（不断变化的）、C exciting（令人兴奋的）、D surprising（令人惊讶的）都承接不了“疲惫—失控”这条线索。

定位 you and your children will benefit and ___ from stressful moments feeling better physically and emotionally。emerge from sth 意为“从……中走出来”，与 feeling better 直接呼应：经历压力之后状态更好。A hide from（躲避）、C withdraw from（退出）都带逃避色彩，与 benefit 矛盾；D escape from 虽可搭配，但强调“逃离”，不如 emerge 贴合“走出来且更好”。

sections.title: Text 1　老鼠与机器鼠交朋友
sections.dir: Read the text and answer the questions by choosing A, B, C or D.
sections.note: 主线：简陋机器鼠只要“会社交”，老鼠就愿意救它。24 题问的是 Wiles，别与 Quinn 的观点混。

paras.en: Rats and other animals need to be highly attuned to social signals from others so they can identify friends to cooperate with and enemies to avoid. To find out if this extends to non-living beings, Laleh Quinn at the University of California, San Diego, and her colleagues tested whether rats can detect social signals from robotic rats.
paras.zh: 老鼠和其他动物必须对来自他者的社交信号高度敏感，才能分辨出可以合作的朋友和需要避开的敌人。为了弄清这种能力是否也延伸到非生命体，加利福尼亚大学圣迭戈分校的拉莱·奎因及其同事检验了老鼠能否察觉机器鼠发出的社交信号。

paras.en: They housed eight adult rats with two types of robotic rat— one social and one asocial—for four days. The robot rats were quite minimalist, resembling a chunkier version of a computer mouse with wheels to move around and colorful markings.
paras.zh: 他们把八只成年老鼠与两类机器鼠——一类“社交型”、一类“非社交型”——同住四天。这些机器鼠极其简陋，像是装有轮子、身上带彩色标记的、更笨重一些的电脑鼠标。

paras.en: During the experiment, the social robot rat followed the living rats around, played with the same toys, and opened cage doors to let trapped rats escape. Meanwhile, the asocial robot simply moved forwards and backwards and side to side.
paras.zh: 实验期间，社交型机器鼠跟着活老鼠四处走动，和它们玩同样的玩具，还会打开笼门让被关住的老鼠逃出来。而那只非社交型机器鼠只是前后左右地移动。

paras.en: Next, the researchers trapped the robots in cages and gave the rats the opportunity to release them by pressing a lever. Across 18 trials each, the living rats were 52 per cent more likely on average to set the social robot free than the asocial one. This suggests that the rats perceived the social robot as a genuine social being, says Quinn. The rats may have bonded more with the social robot because it displayed behaviors like communal exploring and playing. This could lead to the rats better remembering having freed it earlier, and wanting the robot to return the favour when they get trapped, she says.
paras.zh: 接下来，研究者把机器鼠关进笼子，给老鼠们按压杠杆放出它们的机会。在各自 18 轮试验中，活老鼠放出社交型机器鼠的可能性平均比放出非社交型的高出 52%。奎因说，这表明老鼠把社交型机器鼠当成了真正的社交对象。老鼠可能与社交型机器鼠联结得更深，因为它表现出共同探索、共同玩耍这类行为。她说，这可能使老鼠更清楚地记得自己先前放走过它，并在自己被关住时希望它回报这份好意。

paras.en: "Rats have been shown to engage in multiple forms of reciprocal help and cooperation, including what is referred to as direct reciprocity where a rat will help another rat that has previously helped them," says Quinn.
paras.zh: 奎因说：“已有研究表明，老鼠会进行多种形式的互助与合作，其中包括所谓的‘直接互惠’——一只老鼠会帮助此前帮过它的另一只老鼠。”

paras.en: The readiness of the rats to befriend the social robot was surprising given its minimal design. The robot was the same size as a regular rat but resembled a simple plastic box on wheels. "We'd assumed we'd have to give it a moving head and tail, facial features, and put a scent on it to make it smell like a real rat, but that wasn't necessary," says Janet Wiles at the University of Queensland in Australia, who helped with the research.
paras.zh: 考虑到机器鼠的设计如此简陋，老鼠愿意与它交好令人意外。这只机器鼠与普通老鼠大小相同，外形却不过是一个带轮子的塑料盒子。澳大利亚昆士兰大学的珍妮特·怀尔斯参与了这项研究，她说：“我们本以为必须给它装上会动的头和尾巴、面部特征，还要给它涂上气味，让它闻起来像真老鼠，但结果并不需要。”

paras.en: The finding shows how sensitive rats are to social cues, even when they come from basic robots, says Wiles. Similarly, children tend to treat robots as if they are fellow beings, even when they display only simple social signals. "We humans seem to be fascinated by robots, and it turns out other animals are too," says Wiles.
paras.zh: 怀尔斯说，这一发现表明老鼠对社交线索有多么敏感，即便这些线索来自最基础的机器人。同样，孩子也往往把机器人当作同伴，即便它们只表现出简单的社交信号。怀尔斯说：“我们人类似乎对机器人着迷，而事实证明其他动物也是如此。”

items.stem: Quinn and her colleagues conducted a test to see if rats can
opts: pick up social signals from non-living rats
distinguish a friendly rat from a hostile one
attain sociable traits through special training
send out warning messages to their fellows
items.exp: 定位第一段末句 tested whether rats can detect social signals from robotic rats：see if 即 whether，detect 即 pick up，robotic rats 即 non-living rats，逐项都能对上，故 A。B 是同段前半句交代的“老鼠本来的能力”，并非本次实验要检验的东西；C 的 special training 与 D 的 warning messages 文中均无依据。

items.stem: What did the asocial robot do during the experiment?
opts: It set the trapped rats free.
items.exp: 定位第三段末句 Meanwhile, the asocial robot simply moved forwards and backwards and side to side——只是独自前后左右地动，故 D（moved around alone）。A、B、C 三条全都是社交型机器鼠的动作（followed the living rats、played with the same toys、opened cage doors），属张冠李戴，其中 C 更是把“开笼门”安到了非社交型身上。

items.stem: According to Quinn, the rats released the social robot because they
opts: tried to practice a means of escape
expected it to do the same in return
items.exp: 定位第四段末句 wanting the robot to return the favour when they get trapped——老鼠指望自己被关住时对方也来救它，即期待“对方同样回报”，故 B。A 把“回报”曲解为“练习逃生手段”；C 的 display their intelligence、D 的 interesting game 都是把互动当成玩乐，与“直接互惠”这一解释相反。

items.stem: James Wiles notes that rats
opts: can remember other rats' facial features.
respond more to actions than to looks.
can be scared by a plastic box on wheels.
items.exp: 定位第六段怀尔斯的话：原以为必须给机器鼠装上会动的头尾、面部特征、气味，“but that wasn't necessary”。不必有“长相”，老鼠照样认它，说明老鼠对“行为”的反应强于“外貌”，故 C。A 与“面部特征并不必要”相反；B 把“气味也不必要”读成嗅觉更灵；D 的 scared 文中无据。

items.stem: It can be learned from the text that rats
opts: appear to be adaptable to new surroundings
are more socially active than other animals
behave differently from children in socializing
are more sensitive to social cues than expected
items.exp: 定位末段首句 The finding shows how sensitive rats are to social cues, even when they come from basic robots，而第六段的 surprising 与 We'd assumed...but that wasn't necessary 正说明这种敏感超出预期，故 D。A 把“对社交线索敏感”偷换为“适应新环境”；B 的比较级无依据，文中只说人类也如此；C 与 children tend to treat robots as if they are fellow beings 的“相似”相反。

sections.title: Text 2　CEO 高薪是否离谱
sections.dir: Read the text and answer the questions by choosing A, B, C or D.
sections.note: 主线：作者为高薪辩护——人才稀缺、岗位变难，而非“宰客”。28 题的 despite 是转折锚点。

paras.en: It is true that CEO pay has gone up—top ones may make 300 times the pay of typical workers on average, and since the mid-1970s, CEO pay for large publicly traded American corporations has, by varying estimates, gone up by about 500%. The typical CEO of a top American corporation now makes about $18.9 million a year.
paras.zh: CEO 的薪酬确实涨了——顶尖者所得可能是普通员工平均薪酬的 300 倍；而且自 20 世纪 70 年代中期以来，按不同估算，美国大型上市公司的 CEO 薪酬上涨了约 500%。美国顶尖公司 CEO 的典型年薪如今约为 1890 万美元。

paras.en: The best model for understanding the growth of CEO pay is that of limited CEO talent in a world where business opportunities for the top firms are growing rapidly. The efforts of America's highest-earning 1% have been one of the more dynamic elements of the global economy. It's not popular to say, but one reason their pay has gone up so much is that CEOs really have upped their game relative to many other workers in the U.S. economy.
paras.zh: 理解 CEO 薪酬增长的最佳模型是：在一个顶尖公司的商业机会迅速增多的世界里，CEO 人才是有限的。美国收入最高的 1% 人群的努力，一直是全球经济中较有活力的因素之一。这话不讨喜，但他们薪酬涨了这么多，原因之一是 CEO 相对于美国经济中的许多其他劳动者，确实提升了本事。

paras.en: Today's CEO, at least for major American firms, must have many more skills than simply being able to "run the company." CEOs must have a good sense of financial markets and maybe even how the company should trade in them. They also need better public relations skills than their predecessors, as the costs of even a minor slipup can be significant. Then there's the fact that large American companies are much more globalized than ever before, with supply chains spread across a larger number of countries. To lead in that system requires knowledge that is fairly mind-boggling. Plus, virtually all major American companies are becoming tech companies, one way or another. Beyond this, major CEOs still have to do all the day-to-day work they have always done.
paras.zh: 如今的 CEO，至少对大型美国公司而言，必须具备许多远不止“把公司运转起来”的本事。CEO 必须对金融市场有良好的判断，甚至要懂得公司应如何在其中交易。他们还须比前任具备更好的公关能力，因为哪怕一次小小的失误，代价都可能很大。此外，美国大公司比以往任何时候都更加全球化，供应链分布在更多的国家。要领导这样的体系，所需知识相当令人惊叹。再者，几乎所有美国大公司都在以某种方式变成科技公司。除此之外，大公司的 CEO 还得完成他们一贯要做的全部日常事务。

paras.en: The common idea that high CEO pay is mainly about ripping people off doesn't explain history very well. By most measures, corporate governance has become a lot tighter and more rigorous since the 1970s. Yet it is principally during this period of stronger governance that CEO pay has been high and rising. That suggests it is in the broader corporate interest to recruit top candidates for increasingly tough jobs.
paras.zh: 认为 CEO 高薪主要是“宰人”的流行看法，并不能很好地解释历史。从多数衡量标准看，自 20 世纪 70 年代以来，公司治理已严格、严密得多。然而，恰恰是在治理更严的这一时期，CEO 薪酬居高不下且持续上涨。这说明，为日益艰难的岗位招募顶尖人选，符合公司更广泛的利益。

paras.en: Furthermore, the highest CEO salaries are paid to outside candidates, not to the cozy insider picks, another sign that high CEO pay is not some kind of depredation at the expense of the rest of the company. And the stock market reacts positively when companies tie CEO pay to, say, stock prices, a sign that those practices build up corporate value not just for the CEO.
paras.zh: 此外，最高的 CEO 薪酬是付给外部人选的，而不是付给“关系亲近的内部人选”，这再次表明高薪并非以公司其他人为代价的掠夺。而当公司把 CEO 薪酬与股价之类挂钩时，股市会作出正面反应，这表明这类做法提升了公司价值，而不只是让 CEO 受益。

items.stem: Which of the following has contributed to CEO pay rise?
opts: The growth in the number of corporations.
The general pay rise with a better economy.
Increased business opportunities for top firms.
items.exp: 定位第二段首句 The best model for understanding the growth of CEO pay is that of limited CEO talent in a world where business opportunities for the top firms are growing rapidly，把“顶尖公司商业机会迅速增多”与“CEO 人才有限”并列作为解释，故 C。A 的 corporation 数量、B 的普遍涨薪、D 的主要经济体合作文中均未提；B 最易误选，但原文强调 CEO 相对其他劳动者 upped their game，不是水涨船高。

items.stem: Compared with their predecessors, today's CEOs are required to
opts: foster a stronger sense of teamwork
establish closer ties with tech companies
items.exp: 定位第三段 large American companies are much more globalized than ever before... To lead in that system requires knowledge that is fairly mind-boggling，与前任相比，今天的 CEO 要驾驭全球化程度高得多的公司，故 D。A 的 teamwork、B 的研发投入文中未提；C 把“美国大公司都在变成科技公司”偷换成“与科技公司建立更紧密联系”，主体错了。

items.stem: CEO pay has been rising since the 1970s despite
items.exp: 定位第四段 corporate governance has become a lot tighter and more rigorous since the 1970s. Yet it is principally during this period of stronger governance that CEO pay has been high and rising。治理收紧本该抑制高薪，薪酬却仍上涨，despite 后正接“严格的治理”，故 B。A 的内部反对、D 的政府警告文中没有出现；C 的保守经营策略与“薪酬高企”无逻辑关联。

items.stem: High CEO pay can be justified by the fact that it helps
items.exp: 定位末段 the stock market reacts positively when companies tie CEO pay to, say, stock prices, a sign that those practices build up corporate value not just for the CEO。股价挂钩能“做大公司价值”，正是高薪的正当性来源，故 D。A 的 status、C 的 efficiency 文中未提；B 的内部人选与 the highest CEO salaries are paid to outside candidates 正好相反，是设的反向陷阱。

items.stem: The most suitable title for this text would be
opts: CEO Traits: Not Easy to Define
items.exp: 定位全篇脉络：首段承认薪酬涨幅，二、三段讲人才稀缺与岗位变难，四、五段逐条反驳“宰客论”（治理更严、外部招聘、股市正向反应），末句落到 build up corporate value not just for the CEO——通篇都在为高薪辩护，故 A。B 只概括“过去与现在”，漏掉作者立场；C 只覆盖第三段；D 的“特质难以界定”文中并未讨论。

sections.title: Text 3　清洁空气区的政治反转
sections.dir: Read the text and answer the questions by choosing A, B, C or D.
sections.note: 主线：马德里的限车区被政治叫停，作者把矛头指向缺位的国家政府。31 题法官的态度是最大陷阱。

paras.en: Madrid was hailed as a public health beacon last November when it rolled out ambitious restrictions on the most polluting cars. Seven months and one election day later, a new conservative city council suspended enforcement of the clean air zone, a first step toward its possible demise.
paras.zh: 去年 11 月，马德里推出针对污染最严重车辆的严格限制措施时，被誉为公共卫生的一座灯塔。七个月、一次选举之后，新一届保守派市议会暂停执行这一清洁空气区，朝它可能的终结迈出了第一步。

paras.en: Mayor Jose Luis Martinez-Almeida made opposition to the zone a centrepiece of his election campaign, despite its success in improving air quality. A judge has now overruled the city's decision to stop levying fines, ordering them reinstated. But with legal battles ahead, the zone's future looks uncertain at best.
paras.zh: 市长何塞·路易斯·马丁内斯-阿尔梅达把反对该区域作为竞选的核心议题，尽管它在改善空气质量方面卓有成效。如今一名法官已否决该市停止征收罚款的决定，下令恢复征收。但官司还在前头，该区域的前景充其量只是不确定。

paras.en: Among other weaknesses, the measures cities must employ when left to tackle dirty air on their own are politically contentious, and therefore vulnerable. That's because they inevitably put the costs of cleaning the air on to individual drivers—who must pay fees or buy better vehicles — rather than on to the car manufacturers whose cheating is the real cause of our toxic pollution.
paras.zh: 在其他弱点之中，城市在只能独自应对污浊空气时必须采取的措施，在政治上有争议，因而脆弱。这是因为这些措施不可避免地把净化空气的成本转嫁给个体驾驶者——他们必须缴费或购买更好的车辆——而不是转嫁给汽车制造商，而后者的作弊才是我们有毒污染的真正原因。

paras.en: It's not hard to imagine a similar reversal happening in London. The new ultra-low emission zone (Ulez) is likely to be a big issue in next year's mayoral election. And if Sadiq Khan wins and extends it to the North and South Circular roads in 2021 as he intends, it is sure to spark intense opposition from the far larger number of motorists who will then be affected.
paras.zh: 不难想象伦敦也会出现类似的逆转。新的超低排放区（Ulez）很可能成为明年市长选举的重大议题。而如果萨迪克·汗获胜，并按他的打算在 2021 年将其扩展到南北环路，那必然会激起多得多的、届时将受影响的驾车者的强烈反对。

paras.en: It's not that measures such as London's Ulez are useless. Far from it. Local officials are using the levers that are available to them to safeguard residents' health in the face of a serious threat. The zones do deliver some improvements to air quality, and the science tells us that means real health benefits — fewer heart attacks, strokes and premature births, less cancer, dementia and asthma. Fewer untimely deaths.
paras.zh: 这并不是说伦敦超低排放区之类的措施毫无用处。远非如此。地方官员正在动用手中可用的手段，在严重威胁面前守护居民健康。这些区域确实带来了一些空气质量改善，而科学告诉我们，这意味着实实在在的健康收益——更少的心脏病、中风和早产，更少的癌症、痴呆和哮喘。更少的过早死亡。

paras.en: But mayors and councilors can only do so much about a problem that is far bigger than any one city or town. They are acting because national governments — Britain's and others across Europe — have failed to do so.
paras.zh: 但市长和市议员们对一个远大于任何一座城市或城镇的问题，能做的只有这么多。他们之所以行动，是因为各国政府——英国的以及其他欧洲国家的——没有去做。

paras.en: Restrictions that keep highly polluting cars out of certain areas — city centres, "school streets", even individual roads — are a response to the absence of a larger effort to properly enforce existing regulations and require auto companies to bring their vehicles into compliance. Wales has introduced special low speed limits to minimise pollution. We're doing everything but insist that manufacturers clean up their cars.
paras.zh: 把高污染车辆挡在某些区域之外——市中心、“学校街”，甚至单条道路——的限制措施，是对如下缺失的回应：没有更大规模的行动去切实执行现有法规、要求汽车公司让其车辆合规。威尔士已推出特殊的低速限值以减少污染。我们什么都做了，唯独没有坚持要求制造商把车弄干净。

items.stem: Which of the following is true about Madrid's clean air zone?
opts: It has been opposed by a judge.
Its fate is yet to be decided.
items.exp: 定位第二段末句 But with legal battles ahead, the zone's future looks uncertain at best——官司在前，前景充其量只是不确定，即“命运尚未定”，故 D。B 是最强干扰项：法官实际是 overruled the city's decision to stop levying fines，站在该区域一边，与“被法官反对”正相反；A 与 despite its success in improving air quality 矛盾；C 文中说的是执法被“暂停”，不是“需要更严”。

items.stem: Which is considered a weakness of the city-level measures to tackle dirty air?
opts: They are biased against car manufacturers.
They prove impractical for city councils.
They are deemed too mild for politicians.
They put too much burden on individual motorists.
items.exp: 定位第三段 they inevitably put the costs of cleaning the air on to individual drivers—who must pay fees or buy better vehicles，成本被压到个体车主身上，故 D。A 与 rather than on to the car manufacturers 相反——吃亏的是车主，不是车企；B 的 impractical 把“政治上有争议”换成“不可行”；C 的 too mild 文中并未评价力度，只说 contentious and therefore vulnerable。

items.stem: The author believes that the extension of London's Ulez will
items.exp: 定位第四段末句 it is sure to spark intense opposition from the far larger number of motorists who will then be affected。spark intense opposition 即“激起强烈抵制”，故 A（arouse strong resistance）。B 把“汗打算连任后扩张”读成“扩张能保证他当选”，因果倒置；C 的改善交通、D 的抑制造车都不是该句内容。

items.stem: Who does the author think should have addressed the problem?
items.exp: 定位第六段 They are acting because national governments — Britain's and others across Europe — have failed to do so：市长与议员只是“补位”，本该出手的是国家政府，而它缺位了，故 D。B 的 Mayors 与 C 的 Councilors 恰是 can only do so much 的地方官员，是本题最像的干扰；A 的居民是受害者，不是责任主体。

items.stem: It can be inferred from the last paragraph that auto companies
opts: should be forced to follow regulations
will upgrade the design of their vehicles
should be put under public supervision
items.exp: 定位末段 require auto companies to bring their vehicles into compliance 与 We're doing everything but insist that manufacturers clean up their cars。作者惋惜的正是“唯独没有强制车企合规”，反推车企本应被强制遵守法规，故 B。A、C 都是把“强制”读成车企自愿改进；D 的 public supervision 文中未提，原文讲的是政府执法。

sections.title: Text 4　务实的 Z 世代
sections.dir: Read the text and answer the questions by choosing A, B, C or D.
sections.note: 主线：Z 世代务实、求稳、怕风险。38 题考 assuage，要靠 done little 反推“缓解”。

paras.en: Now that members of Generation Z are graduating college this spring—the most commonly-accepted definition says this generation was born after 1995, give or take a year—the attention has been rising steadily in recent weeks. Gen Zs are about to hit the streets looking for work in a labor market that's tighter than it's been in decades. And employers are planning on hiring about 17 percent more new graduates for jobs in the U.S. this year than last, according to a survey conducted by the National Association of Colleges and Employers. Everybody wants to know how the people who will soon inhabit those empty office cubicles will differ from those who came before them.
paras.zh: 既然 Z 世代今年春天就要大学毕业——最广为接受的定义说这一代出生于 1995 年之后，前后相差一年左右——近几周来，他们受到的关注持续升温。Z 世代即将走上街头找工作，而劳动力市场的紧张程度是几十年来所未有的。根据美国大学与雇主协会的一项调查，今年美国雇主计划招聘的新毕业生比去年多约 17%。人人都想知道，这些即将坐进空工位的人，与他们的前辈有何不同。

paras.en: If "entitled" is the most common adjective, fairly or not, applied to millennials (those born between 1981 and 1995), the catchwords for Generation Z are practical and cautious. According to the career counselors and experts who study them, Generation Zs are clear-eyed, economic pragmatists. Despite graduating into the best economy in the past 50 years, Gen Zs know what an economic train wreck looks like. They were impressionable kids during the crash of 2008, when many of their parents lost their jobs or their life savings or both. They aren't interested in taking any chances. The booming economy seems to have done little to assuage this underlying generational sense of anxious urgency, especially for those who have college debt. College loan balances in the U.S. now stand at a record $1.5 trillion, according to the Federal Reserve.
paras.zh: 如果说“理所应当”是用在千禧一代（1981 至 1995 年出生者）身上最常见、也未必公平的形容词，那么 Z 世代的关键词是务实与谨慎。研究他们的职业顾问和专家说，Z 世代是头脑清醒的经济实用主义者。尽管毕业时遇上 50 年来最好的经济，Z 世代却清楚经济灾难是什么样子。2008 年危机时他们还是易受影响的孩子，许多人的父母失业、失去毕生积蓄，或两者皆失。他们不想冒任何风险。繁荣的经济似乎并没有怎么缓解这一代人心底那种焦虑的紧迫感，对有大学债务的人尤其如此。据美联储数据，美国助学贷款余额如今达到创纪录的 1.5 万亿美元。

paras.en: One survey from Accenture found that 88 percent of graduating seniors this year chose their major with a job in mind. In a 2019 survey of University of Georgia students, meanwhile, the career office found the most desirable trait in a future employer was the ability to offer secure employment (followed by professional development and training, and then inspiring purpose). Job security or stability was the second most important career goal (work-life balance was number one), followed by a sense of being dedicated to a cause or to feel good about serving the greater good.
paras.zh: 埃森哲的一项调查发现，今年 88% 的应届毕业生在选专业时就考虑到了就业。与此同时，在 2019 年对佐治亚大学学生的一项调查中，就业指导中心发现，未来雇主最令人向往的特质是能够提供稳定的工作（其次是职业发展与培训，再次是鼓舞人心的目标）。工作保障或稳定性是第二重要的职业目标（工作与生活的平衡居首），其次是投身某项事业的使命感，或为更广大的利益服务而心安。

paras.en: That's a big change from the previous generation. "Millennials wanted more flexibility in their lives," notes Tanya Michelsen, Associate Director of YouthSight, a UK-based brand manager that conducts regular 60-day surveys of British youth, in findings that might just as well apply to American youth. "Generation Zs are looking for more certainty and stability, because of the rise of the gig economy. They have troubles seeing a financial future and they are quite risk averse."
paras.zh: 这与上一代人的想法大不相同。英国品牌管理机构 YouthSight 副总监坦尼娅·米歇尔森指出：“千禧一代希望生活中有更多灵活性。”该机构定期对英国青年开展为期 60 天的调查，其结论或许同样适用于美国青年。“Z 世代追求更多的确定性与稳定，因为零工经济兴起了。他们看不到财务上的未来，而且相当厌恶风险。”

items.stem: Generation Zs graduating college this spring
opts: are optimistic about the labor market
are in favor of office job offers
items.exp: 定位首段 the attention has been rising steadily in recent weeks，即公众关注度持续上升，故 D。A 的 abilities 文中未评价；B 与 a labor market that's tighter than it's been in decades 以及下段“极其谨慎”相反；C 把“即将坐进空工位”这一描述读成“青睐办公室岗位”，属无中生有。

items.stem: Generation Zs are keenly aware
opts: what their parents expect of them
how valuable a counselor's advice is
what a tough economic situation is like
how they differ from past generations
items.exp: 定位第二段 Gen Zs know what an economic train wreck looks like，且后面紧接着 2008 年危机中父母失业、失去积蓄的亲身经历，故 C（清楚艰难的经济处境是什么样）。A 的父母期待、B 的顾问建议文中未提；D 的“与前辈有何不同”是公众与研究者在问的问题，不是 Z 世代自己“清楚知道”的内容。

items.stem: The word "assuage"(line 9, para. 2) is closet in meaning to
items.exp: 定位 The booming economy seems to have done little to assuage this underlying generational sense of anxious urgency——经济繁荣也几乎没能对这股焦虑起什么作用。“作用很小”说明 assuage 是“缓解、减轻”，故 relieve。A deepen（加深）与 done little 的逻辑相反；B define（界定）、C maintain（维持）都不能与“焦虑感”构成“减弱”的意思。

items.stem: It can be learned from Paragraph 3 that Generation Zs
opts: give top priority to professional training
have a clear idea about their future job
care little about their job performance
think it hard to achieve work-life balance
items.exp: 定位第三段 88 percent of graduating seniors this year chose their major with a job in mind，且最看重的雇主特质是 secure employment，可见他们对未来职业有明确打算，故 B。A 把“职业发展培训排在第二”说成“最优先”；C 与“看重工作保障”相反；D 把 work-life balance was number one 读成“难以实现”，文中并未评价难度。

items.stem: Michelsen thinks that compared with millennials, Generation Zs are
items.exp: 定位末段 Michelsen 的话：千禧一代 wanted more flexibility，而 Z 世代 are looking for more certainty and stability... they are quite risk averse。不敢冒险即“更不冒险”，故 B。A 的 less realistic 与 clear-eyed, economic pragmatists 相反；C 的 diligent、D 的 generous 文中均无依据，属凭空比较。

sections.title: Section II Part B　选小标题
sections.dir: Read the following text and answer the questions by choosing the most suitable subheading from the list A-G for each numbered paragraph (41-45). There are two extra subheadings which you do not need to use. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)
sections.note: 五段各有一个动作核心：说真话、听、广交、适度赞美、看人下菜。B 与 G 是多余项。
subs: Give compliments, just not too many.
Put on a good face, always.
sections.intro:
Five Ways to Win Over Everyone in the Office

Is it possible to like everyone in your office? Think about how tough it is to get together 15 people, much less 50, who all get along perfectly. But unlike in friendships, you need coworkers. You work with them every day, and you depend on them just as they depend on you. Here are some ways that you can get the whole office on your side.

blocks.en: If you have a bone to pick with someone in your workplace, you may try to stay tight-lipped around them. But you won't be helping either one of you. A Harvard Business School study found that observers consistently rated those who were upfront about themselves more highly, while those who hid lost trustworthiness. The lesson is not that you should make your personal life an open book, but rather, when given the option to offer up details about yourself or studiously stash them away, you should just be honest.
blocks.zh: 如果你对职场里的某个人心怀不满，你可能会试着在他面前闭口不言。但这对你们俩都没有好处。哈佛商学院的一项研究发现，观察者对那些坦率表露自己的人评价始终更高，而那些隐藏自己的人则失去了可信度。要学的并不是把私生活变成一本摊开的书，而是：当你有机会主动透露关于自己的细节，或者刻意把它们藏起来时，你应该选择坦诚。
blocks.exp: 本段以“隐而不说反失信任”立论：those who were upfront about themselves 得分更高，those who hid lost trustworthiness，落点是 when given the option to offer up details... you should just be honest。核心动作是“公开、不隐瞒”，对应 E Reveal, don't hide, information。B（always 摆出好脸色）谈的是表情管理，与本段“披露信息”无关，是最像的干扰项。

blocks.en: Just as important as being honest about yourself is being receptive to others. We often feel the need to tell others how we feel, whether it's a concern about a project, a stray thought, or a compliment. Those are all valid, but you need to take time to hear out your coworkers, too. In fact, rushing to get your own ideas out there can cause colleagues to feel you don't value their opinions. Do your best to engage coworkers in a genuine, back-and-forth conversation, rather than prioritizing your own thoughts.
blocks.zh: 与对自己坦诚同样重要的，是乐于接纳他人。我们常常觉得有必要告诉别人自己的感受——无论是对某个项目的担忧、一个偶然的念头，还是一句赞美。这些都无可厚非，但你也需要花时间听同事把话说完。事实上，急于把自己的想法抛出来，会让同事觉得你不重视他们的意见。要尽力与同事进行真诚的、有来有往的交谈，而不是把自己的想法放在优先位置。
blocks.exp: 本段两处落到“听”：you need to take time to hear out your coworkers，以及 rushing to get your own ideas out there can cause colleagues to feel you don't value their opinions。take time to hear out 正是 slow down and listen，故 F。E 也含“信息”字样，但本段讲的是“接收”而非“披露”，与 41 段构成对照，切勿混用。

blocks.en: It's common to have a "cubicle mate" or special confidant in a work setting. But in addition to those trusted coworkers, you should expand your horizons and find out about all the people around you. Use your lunch and coffee breaks to meet up with colleagues you don't always see. Find out about their lives and interests beyond the job. It requires minimal effort and goes a long way. This will help to grow your internal network, in addition to being a nice break in the work day.
blocks.zh: 在工作环境中有个“格子间伙伴”或特别信任的知己很常见。但除了这些可信赖的同事，你还应拓宽视野，去了解你周围所有的人。利用午餐和喝咖啡的休息时间，去见见那些你平时不常遇到的同事。了解他们在工作之外的生活与兴趣。这几乎不费什么力气，却能起很大作用。除了是工作日里不错的休息，这还有助于扩展你的内部人脉。
blocks.exp: 本段劝人不要只守着 cubicle mate 或 confidant，而要 expand your horizons and find out about all the people around you，并给出 lunch and coffee breaks 的具体做法，即“与所有人都花点时间”，故 D（Spend time with everyone）。A 的赞美是下一段的内容，属串段；G 的“设身处地”文中没有依据。

blocks.en: Positive feedback is important for anyone to hear. And you don't have to be someone's boss to tell them they did an exceptional job on a particular project. This will help engender good will in others. But don't overdo it or be fake about it. One study found that people responded best to comments that shifted from negative to positive, possibly because it suggested they had won somebody over.
blocks.zh: 正面反馈对任何人来说都值得一听。而且你不必是某人的上司，才能告诉他他在某个项目上做得格外出色。这有助于在他人心中赢得好感。但不要做得过头，也不要虚情假意。一项研究发现，人们对“由负面转为正面”的评价反应最好，这可能是因为它暗示自己已经赢得了某人的认可。
blocks.exp: 本段主题是正面反馈：Positive feedback is important、tell them they did an exceptional job，随即用 But don't overdo it or be fake about it 收束，即“要赞美，但别过头”，与 A（Give compliments, just not too many）严丝合缝。D 的“与所有人相处”是上一段的落点；B 的“始终摆出好脸色”恰好落在被否定的 be fake 一侧。

blocks.en: This one may be a bit more difficult to pull off, but it can go a long way to achieving results. Remember in dealing with any coworker what they appreciate from an interaction. Watch out for how they verbalize with others. Some people like small talk in a meeting before digging into important matters, while others are more straightforward. Jokes that work on one person won't necessarily land with another. So, adapt your style accordingly to type. Consider the person that you're dealing with in advance and what will get you to your desired outcome.
blocks.zh: 这一条或许更难做到，但它能大大推动结果。与人打交道时，要记住对方在互动中看重什么。注意他们如何与他人交谈。有些人在进入正题前喜欢在会议上闲聊几句，另一些人则更直接。对一个人有效的玩笑，未必对另一个人管用。所以，要据此调整你的风格，以适应对方的类型。提前考虑你要打交道的人，以及什么能帮你达成想要的结果。
blocks.exp: 本段要求因人而异：Watch out for how they verbalize with others、Some people like small talk... while others are more straightforward、adapt your style accordingly to type，落点是“按对象调整互动方式”，故 C（Tailor your interactions）。G 的“设身处地”最多只对应 Consider the person，未覆盖“改变自己的风格”这一核心动作，是本题最强干扰。

sections.title: Section III　翻译
sections.dir: Translate the following text into Chinese. Write your translation on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)
sections.note: 按句给分：切句→定主谓→调语序。how to look at it 与 only if we let them 最难。

paras.en: It's almost impossible to go through life without experiencing some kind of failure. People who do so probably live so cautiously that they go nowhere. Put simply, they're not really living at all. But, the wonderful thing about failure is that it's entirely up to us to decide how to look at it.
paras.zh: 人的一生几乎不可能不经历某种失败。不曾经历失败的人，多半活得过于谨小慎微，以致哪儿也去不了。简言之，他们其实并没有真正在生活。不过，失败的可贵之处在于：如何看待失败，完全由我们自己决定。

paras.en: We can choose to see failure as "the end of the world". Or, we can look at failure as the incredible learning experience that it often is. Every time we fail at something, we can choose to look for the lesson we're meant to learn. These lessons are very important; they're how we grow, and how we keep from making that same mistake again. Failures stop us only if we let them.
paras.zh: 我们可以把失败看成“世界末日”，也可以把失败看成它常常本就是的那种难得的学习经历。每当我们在一件事上失败，都可以选择去寻找自己本该从中吸取的教训。这些教训极为重要：我们正是靠它们成长，也正是靠它们避免重蹈覆辙。只有我们自己放任，失败才会把我们拦住。

paras.en: Failure can also teach us things about ourselves that we would never have learned otherwise. For instance, failure can help you discover how strong a person you are. Failing at something can help you discover your truest friends, or help you find unexpected motivation to succeed.
paras.zh: 失败还能让我们认识自己身上那些原本无从知晓的东西。比如，失败能帮你发现自己有多坚强；在一件事上失败，能帮你辨出谁才是真正的朋友，也能帮你找到意想不到的、走向成功的动力。

sections.title: Section IV Part A　应用文（介绍信）
sections.dir: Suppose you are planning a tour of a historical site for a group of international students. Write an email to 1) tell them about the site, and 2) give them some tips for the tour. Do not use your own name, use "Li Ming" instead. (10 points)
sections.note: 两个任务点都要落地：①介绍景点（年代、规模、看点）②2–3 条具体提示。署名固定 Li Ming。
sections.sample:
Dear friends,

I am delighted to tell you that we will visit the Ancient City Wall this Saturday. Built more than six hundred years ago, it runs over thirteen kilometres around the old town and offers a fine view from the top.

Here are a few tips for the tour. Please wear comfortable shoes, as the brick road is uneven and we will walk a long way. Bring a bottle of water and a hat, for there is little shade at noon. And do reach the South Gate by nine o'clock, so that we can set off together.

I look forward to seeing you there.

Yours,
Li Ming
tips: 两个任务点分开写：先介绍景点（年代、规模、看点），再给提示，一段一件事，别揉成一团
提示要具体可执行（wear comfortable shoes / arrive by nine），不要写 enjoy yourself 这类空话
对国际学生用词宜浅显，避免堆砌长难句；开头一句点明写信目的，不要写成通知口吻
署名固定 Li Ming，不写地址、不编造真实姓名

sections.title: Section IV Part B　图表作文
sections.dir: Write an essay based on the chart below. In your writing, you should 1) interpret the chart, and 2) give your comments. You should write about 150 words on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)
sections.note: 图表：某高校学生手机阅读目的——学习知识 59.5%、消磨时间 21.3%、获取信息 17.0%、其他 2.2%。
sections.sample:
The pie chart illustrates why students in a certain university use their mobile phones for reading. Learning knowledge takes the largest share, at 59.5%, followed by killing time (21.3%) and obtaining information (17.0%), while other purposes account for only 2.2%.

Two features stand out. First, study-oriented reading occupies nearly three fifths of the total, which suggests that the phone has become a serious learning tool rather than a mere toy. Second, entertainment and information together still make up about 38%, so the same device serves both study and leisure.

In my view, this distribution reflects the rapid spread of digital reading on campus. Phones put knowledge within reach at any moment, and students naturally turn to them when a question arises. Yet convenience has a price: fragmented reading may weaken concentration. Students should therefore treat the phone as a supplement, not a substitute, for careful reading.
tips: 第一段只做“读数”：最大块 59.5% + 次大 21.3% + 最小 2.2%，不要插入评论
第二段做归并：把“消磨时间 + 获取信息”合成约 38%，与“学习知识”近六成对照，结构最清楚
第三段归因 + 一句提醒（碎片化阅读削弱专注），不要再开新论点
“学习知识占近六成”是全文立论的支点，务必点明，否则图表等于没读
